Fact: Shkolnik et al., Nature 1980 - black and white Bedouin robes gave the same heat gain to the body; black robe surface ~6 C hotter; loose black robe heats the air inside, it rises out the neck and pulls air in from below.

lines.text: The hottest day of the year. Wren wears white, Bram wears black. Who cooks first?
Everyone says Bram. White bounces sunlight away; black soaks it up.
And yes, his robe gets six degrees hotter outside.
But in nineteen eighty, scientists measured the heat reaching the body.
Black robe, white robe: exactly the same.
Here's the trick: his robe is loose.
Hot black cloth heats the air inside, and hot air rises out the neck.
That pulls cool air in from below: a breeze, under his robe.
Wear it tight, and the breeze stops. Then Bram cooks.
